verses.svabodhasiddhi_svab-p01_1: Bow to the giver of freedom, made of every blessing — to Śiva, the sun that burnt away the darkness on every road of becoming.
verses.svabodhasiddhi_svab-p01_2: I praise the highest Śiva — sick with no possession by any creed, to be known only by the feeling of the self, dwelling in himself.
verses.svabodhasiddhi_svab-p01_3: Bow, let there be bow, to Śambhu — smasher of the net of fancies and their floods, standing past even the highest bliss.
verses.svabodhasiddhi_svab-p01_4: Victorious are Śambhu's feet: they teach the wandering world to tell the real from the sham, and wake the knowledge that frees.
verses.svabodhasiddhi_svab-p01_5: Mind, thought, ego, breaths, the senses' subtle fuel and life — all turn back when they see the one worth worshipping, whom we worship.
verses.svabodhasiddhi_svab-p01_6: I bow — I — to pure awareness: the only knife that cuts the heart's knot of 'mine' and 'I', that swallowed throbbing and its stillness both.
verses.svabodhasiddhi_svab-p02_7: How tell what cannot be named? If anyone reaches it at all, it is by the honest method of feeling oneself.
verses.svabodhasiddhi_svab-p02_8: Taught the yoga of knowing, yet with no trust inside — trustless, how could he ever taste freedom's fruit?
verses.svabodhasiddhi_svab-p02_9: The way to the goal is this: stay awake in your own awakening. From such waking the sage stands whole, undivided.
verses.svabodhasiddhi_svab-p02_10: No way but keeping to your own being. Keep to her, rest in yourself — whoever does is happy.
verses.svabodhasiddhi_svab-p02_11: From noticing your own notions, from holding to pure knowing, from winning the highest joy — the sage grows one solid mass of waking.
verses.svabodhasiddhi_svab-p02_12: Grip your notions still, and power comes to rest in the powerful; their oneness is what yogis are after.
verses.svabodhasiddhi_svab-p02_13: Know your own form, drop the veil of principles, scatter the cause of striving — then, tradition says, you are called free.
verses.svabodhasiddhi_svab-p02_14: With a fully wakened mind, hold to waking alone — until, by your own strength, you stand in yourself, alone.
verses.svabodhasiddhi_svab-p03_15: Ever fully awake, he sees himself by himself; for the seer settled in his own form, what else is left?
verses.svabodhasiddhi_svab-p03_16: To be always fully awake is for the mind to waste away; from that wasting, yogis truly see.
verses.svabodhasiddhi_svab-p03_17: Turned back into self-awareness, with no twoness left — he is king among yogis, a sun against the dark of ignorance.
verses.svabodhasiddhi_svab-p03_18: The moon pales before the joy of tasting your own nature; with the inner organ gone, what is there left for me to get?
verses.svabodhasiddhi_svab-p03_19: Self-knowledge and rest, firm and bright, for whoever holds them; freed from the mind's whirl, aloneness comes soon.
verses.svabodhasiddhi_svab-p03_20: For yogis grounded in themselves, whose single mind sweeps aside the traces of grasping and the grasped — fortune's release is easy.
verses.svabodhasiddhi_svab-p03_21: Rest in my own form I have won, my sorrows ended, the split of grasped and grasper broken — I stand firm, abiding as I am.
verses.svabodhasiddhi_svab-p03_22: Whether up and about or gathered inward, whoever wins that nondual, wakened taste of his own nature knows what is real.
verses.svabodhasiddhi_svab-p03_23: For one whose self-standing never slips in any state — what can the squabbles of scripture-rangers do to him?
verses.svabodhasiddhi_svab-p03_24: His self freed from the delusion brewed of real and unreal notions — he lives on among people, fear gone, always a yogi.
verses.svabodhasiddhi_svab-p04_25: Senses cast off, having sat with absorption even once — the highest stands face to face with the yogi whose work is done.
verses.svabodhasiddhi_svab-p04_26: Unbroken in the I-self, gathered by his own effort — may he wake, and stand in himself, till he shines as Sadāśiva.
verses.svabodhasiddhi_svab-p04_27: His turning partless, all objects dropped, the knower who won the winning, aimed at waking alone, standing in himself — indeed he casts off his own sheath, the yogi.
verses.svabodhasiddhi_svab-p04_28: Whose honest method is the word and the taste, unbroken in self-awareness — he is fit to make teaching, and to wake pupils rightly.
verses.svabodhasiddhi_svab-p04_29: From wanting nothing, from self-waking, from dropping hope and pride, from cutting the road of real-and-unreal — no taking of a body again.
verses.svabodhasiddhi_svab-p04_30: Inner sense at peace, fancies thinned, delighting in the gain of his own form, drunk on the nectar of tasting himself — he goes to freedom, his work done.
verses.svabodhasiddhi_svab-p04_31: So, for reaching the goal — stainless, lighting consciousness, true, mother of freedom's rise — I have told the perfection of self-waking.
verses.svabodhasiddhi_svab-p04_32: This teaching can make even one who never won enough, and free him from doubt's fault — with such doubtless teaching, what business has the much-chanting scholar?
verses.svabodhasiddhi_svab-p04_33: All-blessing maker, wildfire to tangled deeds, shower of your own station, free of every notion, temple of all joy — to cut suffering's root I bow to the unmatchably lovely Śiva, taught from the guru's mouth.
